newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE ends at six-week high on Wall St rally.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE ends at six-week high on Wall St rally.

text.p: ** UK shares advance after U.S. data calms fears
of near-term U.S. rate rise and Dow rallies in response.
** Gilts end firm, tracking strong gains in T-bonds.
** Dow trades 101 pts higher as London markets close.
** Financials lead gainers, funds increase sector weighting.
"The financials have been largely responsible for driving us higher and most of today's gains came from the States and rethinking on interest rates," the dealer said.

Attention was fixed on events across the Atlantic for much of the day, despite the proximity to the UK election on Thursday, as investors became increasingly worried over the possibility of rising interest rates both at home and abroad.
Dealers said fears of a U.S. rate hike were calmed after the latest U.S. employment cost index and durable goods orders came in weaker than anticipated and the market rallied as a result.
UK shares were up just 7.5 points ahead of the news.
Investors were reluctant to take any risks in front of the potentially market-moving data.
But the figures were well received. A surge in U.S. bonds led to a sharply higher start for the Dow and UK shares rallied to the day's best levels.
The Dow was 101 points higher as London markets closed.

The data included the first quarter Employment Cost Index which rose 0.6 percent compared with forecasts of around 0.9 percent and March durable goods orders, which fell by an unexpected 3.0 percent against forecasts it would remain flat.
The June gilt future settled up 20/32 at 109-22.

"I still don't think we're out of the woods yet," said Stuart Weatherby, economist at Panmure Gordon. "I'll be looking at NAPM and payrolls data at the end of the week before I'm convinced the economy is slowing, but its certainly less likely now that we'll see a U.S. rate rise on May 20."

The more up-to-date employment report on Friday is seen by analysts as likely to have a stronger influence over U.S. policy decisions. Domestic interest rate sentiment also improved on Tuesday after consumer credit figures came in weaker-than-expected, helping to build expectations that the next UK rate rise will be no more than a quarter point.
Among individual shares, financial stocks continued to feature as investment funds increased their sector weightings building societies.
"Banks and insurers have been running quite hard and that is the real strength in the index," said one senior equity dealer.
Barclays finished 47p higher at 11.63-1/2 stg, National Westminster added 35p to 753-1/2p and Abbey National put on 26-1/2p to 852-1/2p.
Among insurers, Legal & General was up 23p at 431-1/2 and General Accident was up 24-1/2p at 876-1/2p.
Elsewhere, printing group Watmoughs was the biggest percentage loser of the day, when the shares plummeted 90p to 270 after the company issued a profit warning.

Stores group Sears was among the most actively traded stocks in volume of 24 million though the shares were unchanged at 77-1/2p. The group announced it was demerging its department store Selfridges and selling the Freemans mail order business to Littlewoods for 367.5 million stg.
The Mid-250 index ended 10.8 points higher at 4,507.0 and the Reuters/HSBC 150 index finished 10.97 firmer at 1,189.95.
-- Elaine Hardcastle, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4027
